articles.title: España gana el oro en el relevo mixto de las Series Mundiales de Abu Dabi
articles.standfirst: Es la primera vez en la historia que el equipo español del relevo mixto se impone en una prueba de este nivel
articles.summary: Es la primera vez en la historia que el equipo español del relevo mixto se impone en una prueba de este nivel
articles.body: El cuarteto español integrado por Sara Guerrero, Antonio Serrat, Marta Pintanel y David Cantero se impuso en la prueba del relevo mixto de la etapa de las Series Mundiales de triatlón disputada en Abu Dabi. Los triatletas españoles, que habían tenido un buen comportamiento en las pruebas individuales, volvieron a repetir una buena actuación y estuvieron durante toda la competición en los puestos de privilegio. Con todo por decidirse, , Cantero, todo un especialista en la carrera a pie, fue el encargado de luchar por entrar en el podio. Tras recoger el testigo en la quinta plaza supo jugar sus cartas y dio la puntilla a sus rivales con un tremendo cambio de ritmo justo antes de entrar en la última recta al que no pudieron responder sus oponentes, el australiano Luke Willian y el brasileño Manoel Messias. "Intenté concentrarme en la natación y mantenerme en cabeza el mayor tiempo posible. Cuando Luke se escapó, no logramos organizarnos, pero sabía que el circuito de carrera a pie sería rápido, así que jugué mis cartas de la mejor manera posible. Al ver que Max tenía una penalización pendiente, me sentí con total confianza para asegurar la victoria", afirma Cantero. Imparable y pletórico, certificó en Hydayriyat Island el triunfo español con un crono de 1h18:14, con dos segundos de ventaja sobre Australia, seis sobre Brasil y trece sobre Rusia y Alemania.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes Posts CM Punk's Funny Wish List for WWE Survivor Series, Sgt. Slaughter Responds
articles.summary: A WWE Hall of Famer chimed in on Saturday after Cody Rhodes posted CM Punk's list of suggestions for their Team USA squad at Survivor Series.
articles.body:
A WWE Hall of Famer chimed in on Saturday after Cody Rhodes posted CM Punk's list of suggestions for their Team USA squad at Survivor Series.

During Friday night's episode of SmackDown, Punk handed Rhodes a piece of paper on which he had written some ideas for the Survivor Series team. Rhodes subsequently posted a photo of the list on X:

Stars Who Could Make Shock Return at Survivor Series 😮

Punk made several humorous recommendations, including Sgt. Slaughter, which he wrote as "Es Gee Tee Slaughter."

On Saturday, Slaughter replied to Rhodes' post, suggesting that he would be willing to help, while also expressing bewilderment at Punk writing "Es Gee Tee."

Of course, Punk was humorously referencing a video featuring WWE women's champion Tiffany Stratton that went viral over the summer.

In the video, Stratton opened a pack of Topps cards and read off the names. When she got to Sgt. Slaughter, Stratton pronounced Sgt. as "Es Gee Tee" rather than "sergeant."

At Survivor Series on Nov. 28, there will be a traditional, five-on-five, elimination match pitting Team USA vs. Team Mexico.

Rhodes, Punk and Je'Von Evans have been named to Team USA thus far, while Team Mexico is comprised of Rey Mysterio, Penta and Rey Fenix.

Slaughter's addition to Team USA seems unlikely given that he is 78 years old and long retired from in-ring competition, but he undoubtedly would have been a great fit for the team in his heyday.

articles.title: Austin Cindric Wins Veterans Classic At Daytona Beach
articles.summary: Austin Cindric secured a military victory on Wednesday, beating Robert Noaker in a tight race. The win sets the tone for the historic 24-hour event starting...
articles.body:
Austin Cindric proved he can still win at Daytona Beach on Wednesday night. At the first Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic, he claimed the checkered flag. This 30-minute exhibition race featured 12 Ford-affiliated drivers in Mustang Dark Horse Rs. Cindric started from the pole and held off a fierce late challenge from Robert Noaker. The pair swapped the lead three times in the final minutes before Cindric made the winning pass. Noaker, who represents the Marine Corps, finished second. Ryan Preece took third for the Navy. Cindric joked about his win in Victory Lane, saying, according to Speedway Digest , "I finally have something to put on the center of the Christmas card, so I did win a race this year after all the talk." He noted that the event was a great way to honor the veterans and the Air Force.

A Clean Battle for Military Bragging Rights

The race had no championship points, but the bragging rights were huge for the military branches. It was a rare sight in stock car racing to see such close driving end safely. Noaker said he knew Cindric would race clean, and it was fun to compete that close. "It was a blast to race Austin," Noaker said. "I knew he was gonna race clean. He probably knew I was gonna race clean and it was so much fun to race that close and not have any contact and put on a great show for all the veterans here tonight." This clean finish showed that respect matters more than just winning the trophy.

Very few races remain at the World Center of Racing that Cindric has not won. He admitted he still wants to conquer the truck race and the Rolex 24. "There's only two races at Daytona I've entered, this is a subtle brag, that I haven't won and it's the truck race and it's the Rolex 24," Cindric said. While Cindric chases his next win, the track prepares for a massive historic return. The legendary Sunbeam 1000hp will come back to Daytona Beach in 2027. On those sands, Sir Henry Segrave set a world land speed record of 203.792 mph, an event marking 100 years. The car is coming back after a three-year restoration by the National Motor Museum. Jon Murden, Chief Executive of the museum, said, according to SpeedwayMedia.com , "To be able to take this iconic car back to Daytona Beach, where World Land Speed Record history was made, will be incredible – especially in the centenary year."

On Saturday at 2:00 p.m., the HSR Classic Daytona 24 Hour presented by Mission Foods begins.

articles.title: Aiden Flora runs for 216 yards and fuels fast start in Cyclones' 41-13 win over Cincinnati
articles.summary: AMES, Iowa (AP) — Aiden Flora ran 28 times for 216 yards and Iowa State's first three touchdowns, and the Cyclones rode a fast start to a 41-13 victory over...
articles.body:
AMES, Iowa (AP) — Aiden Flora ran 28 times for 216 yards and Iowa State's first three touchdowns, and the Cyclones rode a fast start to a 41-13 victory over Cincinnati on Saturday.

The Cyclones (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) piled up 551 total yards for their fourth game over 500 and improved to 5-1 at home.

The Bearcats (5-5, 2-5) have lost six road games in a row and 12 straight November games since 2023.

Flora ran 10 times for 125 yards and three touchdowns, caught two passes for 19 yards and completed a pass for 37 — all in the first quarter. He joined BYU's LJ Martin as the only players to rush for three TDs in a first quarter this season.

Flora has gone over 200 yards rushing three times this season and has had at least 180 in five games. The former walk-on is averaging 206.3 yards in the last three games and 133.5 for the season.

Cincinnati's Cole Tabb broke a 66-yard run on the game's second play from scrimmage to set up the Bearcats' first touchdown and then Flora took over.

His TD runs were from 11, 77 and 5 yards and put the Cyclones up 21-7. He took a direct snap and flipped a pass to tight end Vince Benetti for a 37-yard gain the play before his third touchdown and is now 4-for-4 passing for 85 yards this season.

Tabb finished with 165 yards on 16 carries and caught eight passes for 70 yards. JC French IV was 14 of 23 for 97 yards.

Iowa State's Jaylen Raynor also was 14 of 23 and finished with 229 yards and a TD through the air.

Cincinnati: The Bearcats have lost three in a row and are on another late-season slide under Scott Satterfield. They need one win to reach bowl eligibility a second year in a row.

Iowa State: Cyclones were the preseason pick to finish last in the Big 12 and must win one of their last two games to achieve bowl eligibility in coach Jimmy Rogers' first season.

articles.title: Ole Miss – Oklahoma OPEN THREAD
articles.summary: It’s a must win for the Rebels in a series where Oklahoma has never won
articles.body:
The Ole Miss football team should be taking the field in Norman today ready to forget the embarrassment of last week in a blowout loss to Georgia.

Wide receiver Horatio Fields said in a press conference this week the team was excited to go on the road again attempting to shush the crowd. Head coach Pete Golding said the team didn't play well, and coaches didn't coach well last week leading to a terrible outcome.

Now there's a chance to flush all of that 42-7 loss and somehow keep the Rebels' playoff hopes alive. The handy dandy Allstate Playoff Predictor puts Ole Miss at a 51 percent chance to make the playoff with three wins to cap off this season. At 9-3, the national media is already speaking to one or two SEC teams making the top 12.

Ole Miss likely needs some help though, and the scoreboard watching will happen late into the night on Saturday. Will Tennessee or Texas stumble on the road? Does Florida or Texas Tech log a win in hostile territories? And what unlikely upset comes to fruition to spin everything into chaos the last three weeks?

All the Rebels can control however is the 60 minutes against Oklahoma this afternoon. The Sooners offense has had a slight bump in a positive direction recently while the Ole Miss defense has looked maybe its worst all season in two of the last three weeks.

Trinidad Chambliss has to find his groove again, and offensive playcaller John David Baker has to open things up for the talented signal caller. Go five wide, spread out the field and let the senior use his legs to keep drives alive like we have seen plenty in the past.

The Rebels will be without Kewan Lacy for the remainder of the season, and fans are ready for the Shekai Mills-Knight breakout game to become a reality. The sophomore running back has shown some solid play, and if he can pile up a 100-yard game against a Brent Venables defense, it would only build a boatload of confidence for this offensive line and team.

Kickoff is set for 3:15 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. HYDR, cheers and go to hell OU.

articles.title: Panthers activate Xavier Legette from IR in latest batch of roster moves
articles.summary: With the Carolina Panthers’ matchup against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday afternoon, the team gets a big injury update on wide receiver Xavier Legette, wh...
articles.body:
With the Carolina Panthers ' matchup against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday afternoon, the team gets a big injury update on wide receiver Xavier Legette , who has been out since Week 2 on Sept. 20 with a knee injury. As fans have been awaiting any injury updates for the Panthers receiver in Legette, the latest news signals that a return is in the horizon.

According to ESPN's Carolina reporter, Leggete has been "activated" from the team's injury reserve on Saturday before the NFC South contest against the Saints. However, the team is keeping corner back Mike Jackson, offensive lineman Brady Christensen, and running back Jonathan Brooks on the injured reserve.

"The Carolina Panthers activated wide receiver Xavier Legette (knee) from injured reserve Saturday ahead of Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the New Orleans Saints," Kaye said. "Cornerback Mike Jackson (groin), offensive lineman Brady Christensen (hamstring) and running back Jonathon Brooks (groin) will remain on injured reserve after being listed as questionable heading into the game."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

More on the progress of Panthers' Xavier Legette

The news of the Panthers taking Legette off the injured reserve on Saturday comes after the team activated his 21-day practice window, per Kaye. The same was done for Jackson and Brooks, but the thinking could be that Leggete was farther along in his recovery.

"The Panthers will activate the 21-day injured reserve practice windows for CB Mike Jackson (groin) and RB Jonathan Brooks (groin), along with WR Xavier Legette (knee), today, per a league source," Kaye wrote on X, formerly Twitter. "They also plan to re-sign WR David Moore to the practice squad."

Legette had been dealing with a Grade 1 knee sprain since Week 2 of the season, and so far, he's just recorded two catches for 64 yards. Currently in his third season with Carolina, he was looking to improve after 2025, when he caught 35 passes for 363 yards and three touchdowns.

At any rate, it remains to be seen when Legette makes his return to the field for the Panthers, as the team is 3-5, though they're placed first in the NFC South.

articles.title: Florida State's lowest-graded players in win over Pittsburgh
articles.summary: Despite Florida State's 16-10 victory over Pittsburgh, Pro Football Focus identified several Seminoles who struggled.
articles.body:
Florida State football kept its postseason hopes alive Friday night, defeating Pittsburgh 16-10 at Acrisure Stadium to secure its second consecutive victory under interim head coach Rick Stockstill.

The Seminoles (5-5, 3-4 ACC) relied on another impressive defensive performance to overcome an offense that managed just 260 total yards and one touchdown.

Three of Florida State's five lowest-graded players came from the offensive side of the ball, reflecting some of the challenges the Seminoles faced moving the football against Pittsburgh.

Here are FSU's five lowest-graded players from Friday's victory, according to PFF 's overall offensive and defensive grades.

Parks rounds out the bottom five after receiving a 55.0 offensive grade across 25 snaps. The running back struggled to make an impact on the ground, earning a 54.0 rushing grade and a 57.6 run-blocking grade.

However, his performance wasn't without positives. Parks received an impressive 81.3 pass-blocking grade, highlighting his contributions in protecting quarterback Ashton Daniels.

Brooks finished with Florida State's second-lowest defensive grade, earning a 53.3 across five snaps. The defensive end recorded a 56.7 run-defense grade and a 57.6 pass-rush grade while failing to generate a quarterback pressure.

Kirkland was Florida State's lowest-graded defensive player, earning a 51.6 overall grade across 12 defensive snaps. The defensive back struggled particularly against the run, receiving a 54.2 run-defense grade while earning a 61.9 coverage grade.

Carter received Florida State's second-lowest grade, finishing with a 51.5 across just seven offensive snaps. The wide receiver earned a 57.0 receiving grade, although his limited involvement made it difficult to establish much of an offensive impact.

Despite scoring Florida State's only touchdown, Thomas received the team's lowest overall grade with a 47.7 across 27 offensive snaps. The freshman running back finished with 39 rushing yards on 13 carries, including a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter that gave the Seminoles the lead.

His performance represented a step back statistically after rushing for 98 yards and two touchdowns against Boston College the previous week.

articles.title: Austin Harvey helps Hope football get back on track with win over Trine, playoffs next
articles.summary: The Flying Dutch bounced back from their lone loss for a big win over Trine, giving them big momentum heading into the playoffs.
articles.body:
HOLLAND - Austin Harvey has been one of the top defensive backs in the MIAA - and the Midwest - for the past three years.

The Hope College senior is so good that teams rarely throw his direction.

That is in part why it took until the regular-season finale for Harvey to snag his first interception of the season.

Harvey stepped in front of a Trine pass down the sideline and raced toward the end zone.

He was tackled inside the 5-yard line but it led to a Brody Schuiteman touchdown and propelled the Flying Dutch to a 48-14 win over the Thunder on Saturday, Nov. 14, on senior day.

Hope finished second in the MIAA behind Calvin . Seven different players scored touchdowns on Saturday.

The Hope College football team has hosted playoff games the past two seasons.

After a loss to Calvin, Hope's seniors knew its regular-season finale would really be their final game at Hope's Ray & Sue Smith Stadium.

Hope is almost assuredly headed to the playoffs. The NCAA Division III selection show at 5 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15.

Hope had a huge class of 22 seniors this season.

Before the game, they were honored with their families.

The seniors are Eli VanderVeen, Denny Belmonte, Trevor Griffiths, Alex Thole, Jonny Rohen-Blanton, Tyson Mann, Patrick Rowland, Austin Harvey, Caleb Clinger, Kaden DeHorn, Tyson Williams, Joey Mahaney, Seth Luhmann, Garrett Langmo, Kemper Millis, Owen Sweeney, Tate Bezeau, Phillip McLaurin, Timothy Clay, Ethan Staffke, Brandon Soltis and Jacob Reynolds.

articles.title: 'There is no racism in Spain' says country's World Cup-winning coach
articles.summary: Spain's Luis de la Fuente had a stern response to questions about racial abuse.
articles.body:
England manager Thomas Tuchel does not expect racist abuse during Sunday's Nations League clash with Spain but said his players would be reminded of anti-racism protocols, prompting a terse response from Spain coach Luis de la Fuente.

England face the world champions in Madrid with top spot in their Nations League group at stake, returning to the Spanish capital for the first time since a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were subjected to racist abuse from the crowd.

England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred.

"In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place we followed," Rice told reporters on Saturday. "We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"I'm not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium, the players we're playing against we have a lot of respect for. It's set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one."

The issue gained traction after Spain were fined $20,000 following anti-Muslim chants by supporters during a match against Egypt in Barcelona in March.

Spain must also play their next home friendly with a reduced-capacity crowd as part of the punishment.

Spain celebrates World Cup win with epic parade

Racism not an issue in Spain, De La Fuente says

De la Fuente rejected any suggestion that racism was a problem in Spain.

"What I can tell you, and you can pass this on to Thomas, is that there is no racism in Spain. That's how strongly I feel about it," De la Fuente said.

"There is no racism. Just as in England, there is no racism in Spain. None of us are racist."

Tuchel bristled when told of De la Fuente's remarks, accusing sections of the Spanish media of misrepresenting his comments.

"I was polite enough to (answer) a question from your colleagues, and you run and ask the other coach and tell him that I talk about racism in Spain," Tuchel said.

"I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens. I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on earth."

James Trafford will start in goal for England on Saturday, said Tuchel, who added that everyone was fit to play including Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence who have recovered from injury.

articles.title: Dolphins add 3 players to active roster for Colts clash
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins (1-7) have made three roster moves ahead of their Week 10 road matchup against the Indianapolis Colts (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS,...
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins (1-7) have made three roster moves ahead of their Week 10 road matchup against the Indianapolis Colts (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, adding kicker Zane Gonzalez, quarterback Brady Cook and wide receiver Jalen Reagor to their active roster.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the moves Saturday on X, formerly known as Twitter.

"Dolphins signed K Zane Gonzalez to their active roster, and elevated QB Brady Cook and WR Jalen Reagor to their active roster for Sunday's game against the Colts."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Gonzalez has already served as Miami's kicker for the past three games, converting five of seven field-goal attempts (71.4%) and all five extra-point attempts.

The 31-year-old made three of four field-goal attempts in Miami's 19-9 Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions , including a 52-yarder. He also connected on two of three attempts against the New England Patriots in Week 8, making another 52-yard field goal.

Gonzalez previously converted all four extra-point attempts in Miami's 28-25 Week 7 victory over the New York Jets.

The Dolphins had exhausted Gonzalez's three permitted practice squad elevations, making his signing to the active roster necessary for him to continue handling kicking duties.

Dolphins make roster adjustments ahead of Colts matchup

Miami also elevated Cook and Reagor from its practice squad, providing additional depth at quarterback and wide receiver for Sunday's matchup.

The Dolphins enter Week 10 looking to snap a two-game losing streak following consecutive defeats against the Patriots and Lions.

Despite their struggles this season, Miami's defense held Detroit to 19 points last Sunday, although the offense failed to score a touchdown.

The Colts have also struggled, entering Sunday's contest on a five-game losing streak.

With both teams searching for answers, Miami will look to secure its second victory of the season while Indianapolis attempts to end its own losing streak.

articles.title: UConn football rocks James Madison, 46-22, at Rentschler Field to earn win No. 5
articles.summary: EAST HARTFORD – The UConn football team saw contributions from all three phases in a decisive win over James Madison, 46-22, at Rentschler Field on Saturday....
articles.body:
EAST HARTFORD – The UConn football team saw contributions from all three phases in a decisive win over James Madison , 46-22, at Rentschler Field on Saturday.

Quarterback Kalieb Osborne responded from last week's three-turnover game against North Carolina with an impressive effort that kept the Huskies' bowl hopes alive, completing 16 of 20 passes for 274 yards and three touchdowns, while running 16 times for 88 yards. Senior receiver Shamar Porter made four catches for a career-high 135 yards and a touchdown.

The Huskies (5-5) accumulated 232 of their 506 total yards on the ground, with Cyncir Bowers accounting for 123 on 25 carries. It was his first game this year with both a rushing and a receiving touchdown as he found the end zone twice on the ground, once through the air.

James Madison's record, boosted by the seventh-easiest schedule in the country, according to ESPN , fell to 8-3 on the year.

The win ended UConn's five-game losing streak in the all-time series against the Dukes (JMU leads, 5-2), which included a 44-6 loss in their most recent meeting in 2023. It also brought the Huskies one win away from bowl eligibility with two opportunities remaining as Old Dominion visits for a 3:30 p.m. kickoff on Saturday with the season finale on the road at Wyoming on Nov. 28.

UConn started the scoring on Saturday with a 28-yard field goal from freshman Jack O'Connor before quarterback JC Evans led the Dukes down the field and punched in for a goal line touchdown. They attempted a fake PAT, but fumbled the snap and settled for a 6-3 lead.

Ky Wilson, who's used that nickname since high school, picked a lane on the ensuing kickoff and switched sides of the field, outrunning the entire JMU kickoff team for a 100-yard return. It was UConn's first kick return touchdown since 2024, when Mel Brown went 96 yards against UMass, and only the fifth of 100 yards in program history. Nick Williams had the most recent 100-yard kick return back in 2010 against Rutgers.

UConn forced a 3-and-out and drove down to the JMU 17-yard line, where it faced 4th-and-inches before a critical false start forced Candle to turn to his field goal unit and O'Connor missed wide right from 40 yards, moving to 1-for-6 from 40-plus yards this season.

The Huskies saw another costly penalty on the next drive from their defense, negating an interception on 3rd-and-6 with a roughing the passer call that extended the drive and led to a 16-yard touchdown pass from Evans to Braeden Wisloski, putting the Dukes back in front with two minutes left in the opening half.

Their lead didn't last long. Osborne found Shamar Porter wide open down the sideline with a perfect pass for an explosive 67-yard score. Linebacker Hayden Pegg dove for his second interception in as many games and the Huskies capitalized on a series of JMU penalties to move down the field, ultimately turning to junior Mike Baker for a 21-yard chip shot field goal – the first of his career – to close the half up, 20-13.

Neither offense could get much going in the second half until Osborne fired another great ball, connecting with Cam Abshire for 51 yards down the left sideline on 3rd-and-19. Bowers ran in from nine yards out to make it a two-score game, 26-13 after a failed extra point operation, just before the end of the third quarter.

The Huskies held JMU to a 36-yard field goal, maintaining the two-score difference with 13 minutes left to play. They answered with another touchdown on a 35-yard connection from Osborne to JD Willoughby, who found the end zone for the third time this year, effectively putting the game out of reach for an undisciplined JMU team that was penalized 12 times for 133 yards.

UConn continued to pour it on as Osborne found Bowers for a 2-yard touchdown to go ahead, 39-16, after a missed extra point. JMU got in on a four-yard rush with four minutes left in regulation, but Bowers answered with his third score of the day.

articles.title: How a little-known NHL rule could lead to players serving as officials for games
articles.summary: The situation happened once back in 1983 during a game between the Whalers and Devils.
articles.body:
The good news for the NHL is that officials for their 13 North America-based games on Saturday made it to their destinations without issue. Friday's ground stop order issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has already impacted numerous college football games and forced reassignments of NFL and NBA officials this weekend.

But how would the NHL have reacted if any games were affected by the disruption in air travel?

The NHL has long had rules in place should an official be unable to continue officiating a game due to injury, illness, accident, or "misadventure." Either the game would continue with one fewer official or a spare official would be called into duty, if available.

If circumstances prevent a referee or linesperson from being able to make it to the arena for a game, the NHL would "make every attempt to find suitable replacement officials."

And if that fails? That's where things get fun and interesting.

When NHL players once served as linesmen

Rule 31.11 states that in that case one player would be chosen by each team to serve as the referee or linesperson for the game. The home team's choice would act as referee and visiting team's player would be a linesperson.

It's a wild situation to think about, but it's one that has happened in the NHL.

That exact scenario took place on Jan. 15, 1983 during a game between the Hartford Whalers and New Jersey Devils at the Hartford Civic Center. A snowstorm caused referee Ron Fournier and linesman Dan Marouelli to arrive late after the game got underway. While the teams waited, Whalers defenseman Mickey Volcan, who nursing a hand injury and wasn't going to play, and Devils forward Garry Howatt were chosen to work as linemen until the two officials made it to the rink in the second period.

Linesman Ron Foyt's attendance was not affected as he had flown in the night before. He worked as the referee until Fournier was ready to go.

"All of a sudden, [Whalers coach] Larry Kish said, 'We're going to have a player from each team and you're going to represent our team,'" Volcan told NHL.com in 2013. "So we put on some sweats and black practice jerseys and they called us in to the room prior to the game. We sat down and he [Foyt] went through it with us."

The NHL's executive vice president of officiating, Stephen Walkom, a former NHL ref himself, told The Athletic in March that he couldn't imagine a time when using players as officials — even with Rule 31.11 in place — was a realistic option for the league in order for a game to take place.

"Obviously we can assign who we think was capable of doing the game, but we never want to put our players in jeopardy and not put officials on the ice that we don't think are competent and qualified to work the hockey game," Walkom said. "Like I said, it's a rare thing, but I think at some point in time, in the NHL, through misadventure, weather, sickness, something, you must have had a time where GMs didn't agree on who to put on the ice because of officials not showing up and they had to put a remedy in place in the book to account for having the game covered."

articles.title: For Capitanes head coach Vitor Galvani, G League playoffs laid foundation for 2026-27
articles.summary: "It gives us more confidence in some areas," said Capitanes coach Vitor Galvani.
articles.body:
MEXICO CITY - At the start of the season after the Capitanes made the G League playoffs for the first time in franchise history, things are flowing smoother than usual as coach Vitor Galvani helps guide his ball club to a 3-1 start to their 2026-27 campaign. Not everything went well in the postseason, which Galvani is the first to admit, but it also helped build a foundation to continue the upward trajectory of the Mexican franchise. "It's not that we gave up when we got to the playoffs, but honestly, I take the blame for this," said the Capitanes coach (translation ours). "We didn't have the mindset of 'let's play until the 15th,' which is when you become champions."

And while an early exit in the G League playoffs was by no means a desired outcome, it also prepared the team for this campaign. "It gives us more confidence in some areas," he continued. "Last year, we came in with several ideas about how we wanted to play offensively and defensively. And I think we got 70 percent of it right; the other 30 percent had to change over the course of the season."

"I feel more confident about doing that 70 percent better this year," said Galvani. "At times last year, there were moments when we wondered if this going to work or not, we have more confidence in that now."

"Last year, I told you that our goal was to make the playoffs," said the Capitanes coach. "Now I want to fight for more because I feel confident in our staff and our players, and that we can do it. Now, I don't know, maybe it's the other way around."

"This league that you already know, in one week we could have three NBA players (join a team), and everything changes. So, it's about controlling what's within our control. Doing the training we did today, with lots of energy, really wanting to improve, wanting to talk to one another, and from there, gradually achieving things."

articles.title: Rennie doesn't regret selection after All Blacks stunned by Wales in Nations Championship
articles.summary: CARDIFF, Wales (AP) — Coach Dave Rennie wasn't going to second guess his selection after New Zealand lost to Wales in rugby for the first time in 73 years on...
articles.body:
CARDIFF, Wales (AP) — Coach Dave Rennie wasn't going to second guess his selection after New Zealand lost to Wales in rugby for the first time in 73 years on Saturday.

Wales won a stunning Nations Championship nail-biter 35-28, first by starting each half with two quick tries to make the All Blacks play catchup, and then by holding out wave after wave of attacks for nearly the last half-hour when New Zealand was held up three times over the tryline.

The last year the All Blacks tasted defeat against Wales — 1953 — Edmund Hillary, a New Zealander, had just become the first person to summit Mount Everest.

After the All Blacks sunk Scotland 43-21 last weekend, Rennie made 10 changes, including eight of the starting XV, to give front-liners a breather before facing England and the playoffs.

"We had a good enough side to win," he said. "We had opportunities to win but we weren't clinical enough, so I have no regrets around the side we picked. There's not a lot between certain positions. Whoever wears the jersey bars up."

Rennie didn't hide his disappointment, though, and paid tribute to Wales.

"Massively disappointed (in the result)," he said. "We started both halves poorly. Conceded 14 points quickly. (We were) a little bit disconnected. In the end, we had plenty of possession, territory and opportunity to squeeze them up and pick them off.

"Credit to Wales, they were really clinical when they got their chances and then they defended for massive periods. Wales were passionate. Every time they kept us out they grew and became harder to break down."

In the first half Rennie noted his side turned over the ball nine times, four of them offloads trying to force a pass. That was in response to Wales' 14-0 start inside the first six minutes.

"They ran hard onto the ball and were able to generate lightning quick ball," Rennie said. "We struggled to slow it down. They were able to find space on the edge. They were clinical and their ability to take points was excellent."

First-time All Blacks captain Beauden Barrett, who'd won his previous nine matches against Wales, said the defeat was tough to take.

"We were building a lot of pressure and couldn't convert that into points. We were held up a lot of times. It's frustrating. It felt like a brick wall at times," Barrett said. "You have to give them credit. We gave them opportunities to bring the crowd into the game. That's why it's one of the best places in the world to play. It feels like you're playing 16 or 17."

New Zealand blew a chance to put a big buffer on South Africa in the southern hemisphere standings but owns its fate for making the Nov. 29 final by taking a one-point lead. Next weekend the All Blacks go to Twickenham, where they lost last year, and are likely to recall Codie Taylor, Fabian Holland, Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie and Jordie Barrett.

"We expect a response against England," Rennie said.

articles.title: Zinedine Zidane responds to Kylian Mbappé rumours
articles.summary: France national team head coach Zinedine Zidane was this weekend drawn on the ongoing speculation, pointing towards a cold relationship between he and star s...
articles.body:
France national team head coach Zinedine Zidane was this weekend drawn on the ongoing speculation, pointing towards a cold relationship between he and star striker Kylian Mbappé.

The subject of the rapport between Zidane and Mbappé has dominated the media headlines in France across the week to date.

This comes after it was rumoured that, not only were the pair not getting along, but they had endured a serious falling out during a training session.

Speaking during an exchange with the media earlier this week, Mbappé for his part moved to firmly deny any and all rumours regarding as much.

And this was a lead followed by his new manager on Saturday.

Drawn on the situation during a press conference ahead of France's Nations League meeting with Türkiye this evening, Zinedine Zidane assured:

"I don't understand it, but it's not that big of a deal. That's why I'm not going to get into the debate. I have a coach's relationship with my player, and it's going wonderfully. I can't stop people from saying what they say, but it's nonsense. It's a shame and quite annoying."

articles.title: Rutgers football's offense nonexistent in loss to Nebraska | Analysis
articles.summary: Rutgers football's quarterback situation continues to worsen as a bad season nears its end.
articles.body:
PISCATAWAY – This is the type of season it's become for Rutgers football .

The Scarlet Knights were already without starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan for Saturday's game against Nebraska, and second-string quarterback AJ Surace was a game-time decision.

Surace dressed and went through warmups, but third-stringer Sean Ashenfelder ultimately made his first career start.

Then Ashenfelder suffered an apparent leg injury in the first half, and Surace had to come off the sideline and replace him.

In a season that continues to spiral, the quarterback situation continues to worsen – the offense suffered a result.

The Scarlet Knights got little going on that side of the ball, finishing with 143 total yards of offense in a 31-0 loss to the Cornhuskers at SHI Stadium.

They had 101 rushing yards and averaged 3.1 yards per play.

Greg Schiano's team fell to 2-8 (1-6 Big Ten) with the loss – it has just two games to get through before it can officially begin a crucial offseason.

Greg Schiano, longtime Rutgers football coach, former NFL coach

But Rutgers still needs to get through those two games – at Penn State and home against Michigan State in the finale – and the mounting injuries continue to make it more difficult.

The Scarlet Knights have already lost wide receiver KJ Duff, right guard Kobe Asamoah and safety Chris Joines for the season.

This game wasn't much of a fight – Nebraska, which secured its sixth win and bowl eligibility with a win that snapped a four-game losing streak, pretty much controlled it from the start and finished with 429 yards of offense.

But given the state of the Scarlet Knights right now, that shouldn't come as much of a surprise, especially against a defense that ranks among the best in the Big Ten.

Rutgers' season is inching closer to a painful – literally – end.

articles.title: 'One of the greatest wins' - Wales stun All Blacks to go from no-hopers to heroes
articles.summary: Wales end a 73-year hoodoo against New Zealand with a win hailed as their greatest of all time.
articles.body:
One of the greatest Wales wins of all time.

That is how former captain Sam Warburton described the monumental result against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday.

At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top-ranked side in the world following South Africa's tension-filled loss to France on Friday night.

So no-one gave Wales hope - even Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30-1 during the week.

The question, not of when but can, Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset them since 1953.

That 73-year wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama.

Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy - and relief - to the strains of Yma O Hyd.

That losing run - stretching across 34 matches - has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players.

Warburton himself was part of one of the most successful teams of all time during the Warren Gatland era - but lost all five meetings with New Zealand.

Even the legendary team of the 1970s fell short, although Sir Gareth Edwards was among the Principality Stadium crowd on Saturday to witness history.

How many more will claim in years to come that they were there as well?

Warburton said: "When you think what the fans and this team has been through, from the highs of a Grand Slam seven years ago, down to 12th in the world rankings and a record losing run of any tier-one nation, we've been down in the pits.

"No-one gave Wales a chance; that's why this is one of the greatest Welsh wins of all time.

"Yes, New Zealand had made changes but that was one of the most heroic defensive performances I have ever seen."

Dan Biggar, sat alongside Warburton for host broadcaster ITV, put the result into wider perspective.

"This is not a day for analysis; it's just to celebrate being Welsh," he added.

"That was probably the biggest shock in world rugby since Japan beat South Africa in the 2015 World Cup."

Winston Churchill was prime minister and Queen Elizabeth II had not long had her coronation when Wales last beat the All Blacks in 1953.

Respected rugby commentator Huw Llywelyn Davies attended the game as an eight-year-old with his father, who was writing for the weekly Welsh-language newspaper Baner ac Amserau Cymru.

"I never thought I would see it happen again, not unless I lived to 100," said an emotional Davies, now 81, as he stepped away from the media seats inside the Principality Stadium.

"With everything that has been going in Welsh rugby recently, I didn't think we would beat them this decade, but the way we matched them physically was incredible."

Wales had only come close on a handful of occasions with one-point defeats in 1978, when New Zealand lock Andy Haden infamously dived out of a lineout to gain a match-winning penalty, and then in 2004.

Wales even turned to four New Zealand coaches in Sir Graham Henry, Steve Hansen, Gatland and Wayne Pivac to help break the hoodoo, but none of the quartet could inspire a Test victory over the land of their birth.

So there will be added satisfaction that it was a Welshman who masterminded the long-awaited win.

Steve Tandy's side may not have the household names of teams gone by, nor the winning pedigree, but they had courage when it mattered.

Three times they held up black shirts over the try-line during a second-half defensive effort that at times beggared belief.

Initial statistics had second-row Dafydd Jenkins equalling Thierry Dusautoir's world record of 38 tackles in a single match - also set against New Zealand in 2007.

Jac Morgan and man of the match James Botham also topped 30 tackles, while centre Eddie James and captain Dewi Lake were not far behind.

It earned high praise from former New Zealand captain Sean Fitzpatrick.

A winner in all six meetings with Wales, the ex-hooker has ties to that day seven decades ago when his father Brian made his New Zealand debut.

Observers say he was unlucky not to be awarded a try after he was adjudged to have been tackled just short of the line. How different history might have been.

"New Zealand played well in patches and terrible in others but this is all about Wales," said Fitzpatrick, now a board member of Welsh region Scarlets.

"The way they started the game and took their tries showed the amazing belief they had. But the defensive effort was out of this world."

images.caption: Dafydd Jenkins equalled the world record for number of tackles in a Test match [Huw Evans Picture Agency]
Will any of the 2026 team be honoured as Wales' 1953 match-winner Ken Jones was with a statue in his hometown of Blaenavon? [Huw Evans Picture Agency]

articles.title: Three takeaways from Wisconsin football's horrendous loss to Maryland
articles.summary: The last thing this Wisconsin Badgers program needed was a loss at Maryland.
articles.body:
The last thing this Wisconsin Badgers program needed was a loss at Maryland.

Somehow, in Week 11, that's exactly what happened .

The Terrapins, even without their starting quarterback, were able to pull off a massive 24-21 upset .

In the end, it marked their first set of back-to-back Big Ten wins in three seasons, a statistics that UW is stuck on the wrong side of.

Wisconsin committed just three penalties for 24 yards and somehow lost to a team who had 11 penalties for 111 yards.

To say that's in-excusable would be an understatement. In no world should the Badgers have lost this game to begin with, but that statistic makes things even more eye-opening.

Cardell Williams set a school record with 19 straight completions

When news broke that Sebastian Cheeks wouldn't be playing , it slightly changed Wisconsin's outlook going into this game.

Between the likes of Mason Posa, Cooper Catalano, Matt Jung, and others, they still had more than enough talent to get the job done.

Somehow, a backup quarterback who made his first career start at the school set a program record with 19 straight completions.

Williams finished 21/23 for 183 yards, including a 39-yard touchdown that changed everything.

There's something to be said about going 2/12 on third-down or having seven fewer minutes in terms of time of possession, but there's nothing quite like coughing the football up three times.

The biggest of the game was when Ryan Hopkins was sacked after the two-minute timeout, losing the football in the process.

That set up the go-away 30-yard field goal, and the rest was history.

Contact/Follow @TheBadgersWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Wisconsin Badgers news, notes and opinion. You can also follow Jordon Lawrenz on X @ jordonlaw_pxp .

articles.title: Rapid Reaction: Northwestern falls 28-19, fading late at No. 20 Ohio State
articles.summary: The Wildcats pulled within a point early in the third quarter, but miscues helped the Buckeyes pull away late.
articles.body:
Northwestern (6-4, 3-4 B1G) football continues to spiral, dropping its third straight game on Saturday at No. 20 Ohio State (7-3, 5-2 B1G), 28-19, after getting the game as close as 14-13 in the third quarter. Against a Buckeyes team that had struggled in recent weeks, the Wildcats' late-game mistakes cost them.

Redshirt junior quarterback Nicco Marchiol was 18-for-31 for 225 yards and one touchdown in his second start with the program, while redshirt sophomore Luke Dehnicke led the way receiving with five catches for 88 yards and a last-second touchdown, and redshirt junior running back Caleb Komolafe had 54 yards on 11 carries to lead the ground game.

For Ohio State, freshman quarterback Luke Fahey was 21-for-32 for 201 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. The bulk of his passes went to junior wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, who had 117 yards and a touchdown on 11 catches. Sophomore running back Bo Jackson had 114 yards and a touchdown on 20 carries.

With Ohio State electing to defer the initial possession, Northwestern started on its own 25-yard line. A delay of game before the ball was snapped pushed the Wildcats to the 20, and they managed only three more yards on the ground before punting after three downs.

After a solid punt return got the Buckeye offense started near midfield, Ohio State looked to be rolling into the first points of the game with Jackson going for 19 on the first play of the drive. But after another small gain to Smith, Fahey made his first mistake of the game, throwing the ball off a teammate's helmet; it flew into the air before landing in the hands of redshirt senior defensive back Braden Turner.

After the turnover, Marchiol started finding more success on third downs. The 'Cats went 3-for-4 in such situations on the opening drive, including a big pass to Joseph Himon II for 20 yards along the sideline. After charging past OSU's 30, a sack on third-and-6 stopped the Wildcats at the Ohio State 26, where kicker Jackson Kleather hit one through the uprights for the first points of the game.

With the 'Cats on the board, the Buckeyes got right back to work with gains on their first four snaps of the drive. A false start briefly stalled their momentum before Jackson took two more carries for 15 yards and Fahey found Smith cutting across the field for 22 yards, making him the Big Ten record holder for career receiving yards.

After the end of the first quarter, it took just two plays for the Buckeyes to score. A scrambling Fahey found sophomore RB Isaiah West for the game's first touchdown, making it 7-3 OSU.

After the score, the NU offense looked like it would go three-and-out, but a rolling Marchiol found TE Dehnicke for a 22-yard gain, with 15 more added at the end of the play for a hands-to-the-face call on the OSU defense. The 'Cats weren't able to manage much after that, but Kleather came out to make it 7-6 with a big 46-yard kick.

The Ohio State offense kept chipping away at Northwestern, completing short gains on each pass, and barreling Jackson through the defensive line. At the NU 17-yard line, pass interference was called on graduate DB Ore Adeyi, putting OSU at the 2-yard line. From there, NU made it easy for Jackson. He found a big hole and put the Buckeyes up 14-6 with 2:51 left in the half.

With two minutes left in the half, Northwestern found life when redshirt junior Caleb Komolafe gained 10 yards for a first down, but a holding call on graduate center Jackson Carsello backed them into a hole it couldn't get out of. On fourth-and-5, it opted to punt from midfield. Ohio State let the clock run and entered halftime up 14-6 over Northwestern.

At the half, Marchiol was 8-for-12 passing for 85 yards, while Komolafe had 44 rushing yards on nine attempts and Himon led in receiving with 32 yards on three catches. NU's wide receivers caught only one pass in the half: a 2-yard reception by junior Drew Wagner. For Ohio State, Fahey had completed 11-of-16 passes for 92 yards, throwing a touchdown pass and an interception. Smith caught seven of those passes for 67 yards, while Jackson had 58 yards and a touchdown on nine rushing attempts.

To begin the second half, Northwestern held Ohio State to a three-and-out, but it wasn't without a few scares. After missing Smith downfield on the first down, Fahey launched a perfect deep ball to freshman Chris Henry Jr., but it dropped out of his hands, leaving the Wildcats unscathed.

With the ball back in NU's hands, Komolafe got the first down on two rushes before Marchiol found graduate tight end Alex Honig for a 37-yard gain to the OSU 11. A 3-yard pass to Wagner kept the drive alive on third down, and Marchiol finished it off by diving for the pylon on a 2-yard touchdown run. Kleather was good on the extra-point attempt, cutting the Buckeyes' lead to 14-13 with 10:01 left in the third quarter.

Ohio State's offense answered by gaining yards on the first six plays of its subsequent drive, including back-to-back 16-yard passes from Fahey. On third-and-10, Smith caught a pass just past the first-down marker that was initially called incomplete because it was out of bounds. But upon replay review, the officials controversially determined that Smith had dragged his cleats just enough to overturn the call.

The call would prove crucial. With a fresh set of downs, Ohio State — facing fourth-and-1 at the NU 8-yard line — found senior WR Devin McCuin on a slant route for the touchdown, making it 21-13 after the made PAT with 2:52 remaining in the third quarter.

After a bleak three-and-out, Northwestern was briefly saved when its punt bounced off the back of OSU gunner Devin Sanchez, allowing graduate linebacker Braydon Brus to jump on the ball at the Ohio State 43-yard line.

Then the offenses fell into a lull, going three-and-out on three straight drives. Northwestern had a chance to chip away at the 8-point margin after a 30-yard punt return from Wagner put them at the OSU 44-yard line, but they were unable to make anything of it.

The Buckeyes broke the spell. Jackson began with a 23-yard rush, and Fahey found Smith for a 13-yard gain to get in Northwestern territory. After a big gain by RB Legend Bey, an unsportsmanlike conduct call on the freshman would undo all his work.

But the offense wouldn't be done yet. Northwestern committed a rare turnover with Wagner dropping the punt, giving Ohio State prime field position at the Wildcat 10-yard line. It took two plays for Fahey to find Smith, putting the Buckeyes up 28-13 with 6:33 remaining.

With its back against the wall, Northwestern couldn't find an answer with under five minutes remaining in the game. With the ball back, a roughing-the-passer penalty gave the Wildcats an extra 15 yards, but incomplete passes, two sacks and a near-fumble led to NU turning it over on downs with 3:00 remaining.

The Wildcats recovered a fumble late and found sophomore Luke Dehnicke in the end zone for a last second touchdown, but the game was out of hand by then and Northwestern ultimately fell 28-19.

Next Saturday, Nov. 21, the Wildcats head to the Twin Cities to take on Minnesota. Kickoff is set for 11 a.m. CT.

articles.title: Saints run game looks to continue momentum against Panthers
articles.summary: After a strong rushing performance in Week 9, the Saints get another key backfield piece back but must deal with reshuffling on the offensive line
articles.body:
Sunday sees a battle for first place in the NFC South when the New Orleans Saints host the Carolina Panthers at the Superdome. Both teams come in with records of 3-5, a half-game ahead of the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Atlanta Falcons. The Saints are also getting healthy on the offensive side of the ball, perhaps bad news for the Carolina defensive unit.

Most of this season, the Saints have been unable to run the ball with any effectiveness. This has contributed heavily to slow starts while also reducing the productivity of their passing attack. Like New Orleans, however, the Panthers possess one of the worst rushing defenses in the league. We'll break down that aspect of Sunday's matchup now.

Carolina fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero a few weeks ago in large part because of the team's inability to slow the run. The Panthers gave up 291 rushing yards in a season-opening loss to the Bears, then 157 and 132 in the subsequent two outings. Since then, the Panthers have held four of five opponents to under 90 yards on the ground. In the one game where they didn't, a Week 7 loss to Tampa Bay, the Panthers were pounded down with 258 rushing yards.

Inside linebackers Devin Lloyd and Brian Okereke lead the Panthers in tackles with 54 and 49 stops, respectively. Each was added by Carolina this offseason and has excellent range. Lloyd (4) and Okereke (5) have a combined nine stops for loss, but Okereke will miss his second straight game with a foot injury. Outside linebacker Patrick Jones II is also having a strong year and could see some inside reps in the Panthers 3-4 scheme when they go to bigger fronts. Outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (3 tackles for loss) should also see a bigger role.

Edge rushers Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen are far better pass rushers than run defenders, though Phillips has made some plays in opposing backfields. The Panthers have also struggled to make plays against the run with their up front defenders. Derrick Brown continues to be an imposing force and will be opposite the Saints right side, where Taliese Fuaga (knee) is out for Sunday. However, nose tackle Lee Hunter, along with ends Tershawn Wharton and Bobby Brown III, need to be more consistent at the point of attack.

Panthers safeties Tre'von Moehrig and Nick Scott are each solid against the run. Both have good size, with either capable of playing at the line of scrimmage as an extra linebacker. The Panthers are thin and undersized at cornerback, with Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson out with injuries, further allowing opponents to have success against them with off-tackle runs.

New Orleans has managed 100 rushing yards in a game just three of eight times this season, getting held to fewer than 70 yards in four outings. The Saints are coming off 160 rushing yards against Cleveland, their second-highest output of the season. That was helped greatly by the return of running back Audric Estime and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. Estime rushed for 72 yards, the highest total in 2026 by a Saints runner. More reinforcements could be on the way with Travis Etienne (hamstring) ready to come off injured reserve.

Etienne rushed for 128 yards and 4.3 per carry in three games before getting hurt. Better production is needed, but he'd add burst and explosiveness to the attack. Etienne and Estime should be a quality 1-2 punch. Alvin Kamara has proven that he's still a capable receiver, but has added little as a runner. Kamara has only 157 rushing yards so far with a lowly 3.3 per carry.

Quarterback Tyler Shough actually leads New Orleans with 162 rushing yards. While Shough's legs are an added dimension to the offense, a bonafide threat out of the backfield is desperately needed. Once Etienne returns, he'll be the lead back, but coach Kellen Moore clearly has trust in Estime. Expect them to share carries, with Kamara to be sprinkled in as a pass catcher or in certain situations as a change of pace.

Look for the Saints to focus their running game on the left side behind Banks and guard David Edwards. It's where they had most of their success against the Browns. The right side of an offensive line that has struggled most of the year will see different starters in three new positions against the Panthers.

Center Erik McCoy (biceps) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) are out, likely for at least a few weeks. Despite William Sherman playing well after McCoy was hurt against Cleveland, Kellen Moore will instead slide right guard Cesar Ruiz into the spot with rookie Jeremiah Wright stepping in at guard. Asim Richards or rookie Mason Murphy will play right tackle. Richards has more experience and can play either side, but struggled when he replaced Banks at left tackle. Expect the Saints to use an extra tight end, either Noah Fant or rookie Oscar Delp, as an extra blocker. Sherman will also be used in that role during short-yardage packages.

articles.title: Ohio State gets lift from RBs Bo Jackson, Isaiah West in win over Northwestern
articles.summary: Brianna Mac Kay's instant takeaways from Ohio State's win over Northwestern.
articles.body:
Ohio State football snapped its losing skid with a 28-19 win over Northwestern on Nov. 14 at Ohio Stadium.

The Buckeyes were 0-2 since returning from their off week, falling to USC and Oregon by more than 10 points in both games. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who has taken over for an injured Julian Sayin during this stretch, threw for 201 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in his first win as a starter.

Former Ohio State offensive coordinator Chip Kelly was on the opposite sideline for the first time since winning the 2024 national championship with the Buckeyes. Northwestern's Kelly-ran offense posted 278 total yards while being held to two touchdowns and two field goals.

OSU Buckeyes face Northwestern in college football matchup. See the photos

Here are the game's key moments and takeaways:

Ohio State's sophomore running back duo provides crucial production

Sophomore running backs Bo Jackson and Isaiah West took on a large part of Ohio State's legwork, each finding the end zone and combining for 159 of the Buckeyes' 168 rushing yards.

West rushed for 45 yards on 10 carries, and Jackson posted 114 rushing yards on 20 carries.

Jackson was coming off a two-touchdown outing in the 41-28 loss to Oregon, though after scoring in the first quarter, he recorded just 17 yards the rest of the game. Against Northwestern, Jackson continued to be an asset following his 2-yard touchdown during the second quarter.

Jeremiah Smith breaks Big Ten record early vs Northwestern

Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith officially took the Big Ten all-time receiving yards title with a 22-yard catch near the end of the first quarter. Smith entered just 31 yards off from the record, which Purdue's John Standeford set at 3,788 in 2003.

The record-breaking catch was the fourth of Smith's 11 receptions, a high in the three games Fahey has been at quarterback, and finished with 117 yards.

In the fourth quarter, Smith logged his lone touchdown. He came close to scoring another in the second quarter, but instead had the first pass interference call go his way for the first time since the Purdue game last season. Northwestern defensive back Ore Adeyi was charged with the foul against Smith.

Smith has the record at 3,874 yards with two games remaining in the regular season. A junior, Smith is likely in his final season at Ohio State, as he's expected to declare for the 2027 NFL Draft.

Ohio State improves pass rush, third-down defense

In the past two games, the Buckeyes' opponents had moved the chains 15 times on third down. The Wildcats did convert on third down six times, but their third-down conversion rate was below 40% (6 for 15).

The biggest defensive boost Ohio State got against Northwestern was from the pass rush. After recording just two sacks across the past four games, the Buckeyes sacked Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol five times, with Kenyatta Jackson Jr. leading the team with two.

Ohio State's special teams display mix of positive, negative moments

Ohio State still racked up highs and lows after firing special teams coordinator Robby Discher on Monday.

Wide receiver Brandon Inniss opened the Buckeyes' special-teams play with a punt 17-yard return.

But in the third quarter, Ohio State showed its special-teams cracks, first when multiple Buckeyes allowed a squib kick to pass them on the ground, pinning the offense at its own 17-yard line. During Northwestern's next punt, the ball bounced off the back of cornerback Devin Sanchez's shoulder, and the Wildcats recovered it at Ohio State's 44-yard line.

The Buckeyes made up for their errors when long snapper Dalton Riggs recovered a misplayed Northwestern punt return inside the red zone, leading to Smith's touchdown.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith makes unreal history during Ohio State/Northwestern game
articles.summary: The assumption is that Jeremiah Smith has outgrown Ohio State. In other words, he is too good and destined for greater things. But he still has business to...
articles.body:
The assumption is that Jeremiah Smith has outgrown Ohio State. In other words, he is too good and destined for greater things.

But he still has business to take care of while donning the scarlet and grey. On Saturday, the Buckeyes played against Northwestern at home in Columbus. In the final seconds of the first quarter, Smith pulled off a remarkable feat on one catch. He became the all-time receiving-yards leader in Big Ten history with 3,798-plus yards.

It came on a 22-yard reception thrown by QB Luke Fahey. Smith surpassed Purdue's John Standeford record that he held for 23 years.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

In the process, Smith added to the growing list of accolades he has achieved during his time at Ohio State. Smith has already surpassed Michigan's Braylon Edwards for the most receiving touchdowns in Big Ten history, with 39.

Moreover, Smith leads Ohio State in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns. Furthermore, Smith is tied with Marvin Harrison Jr. for the most 100+ receiving-yard games in program history.

Since his first year, Smith has overdelivered in many ways and become one of the most defining college football players today.

Overall, Smith is projected to be the No. 1 NFL draft pick in 2027. Meanwhile, No. 20 Ohio State is 6-3, and as this story is being published, they lead Northwestern 21-13 at the end of the 3rd quarter. Smith has nine receptions for 94 yards after three.

On Saturday, November 21, the Buckeyes will play Nebraska on the road before facing their all-time rival Michigan on Saturday, November 28, in Columbus.

articles.title: Rice close to signing new Arsenal contract
articles.summary: Arsenal and England midfielder Declan Rice says he is close to signing a new contract with his club.
articles.body:
Declan Rice has confirmed he is close to signing a new contract with Arsenal.

BBC Sport first revealed the midfielder was set to sign a new long-term deal at Emirates Stadium on 7 October, and the 27-year-old, speaking before England's game against Spain on Sunday, said: "A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon and I'm extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and team-mates who put so much energy in to me."

Rice's current deal expires in 2028 but the former West Ham star is now expected to extended his tenure in north London, having arrived from London Stadium in 2023 in a deal worth £105m.

The midfielder's new contract will put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner.

Rice has managed to avoid upheaval during his career and he believes that continuity has helped him to blossom.

"I've been extremely lucky I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career. I always set myself targets, pushing for more," he said.

"I'm extremely Iucky not to have to worry about that stuff as it makes playing football far more easier."

articles.title: Rocky Run takes over Philadelphia
articles.summary: 30,000 runners gathered at the Philadelphia Museum of Art for the 2026 Rocky Run Saturday morning.
articles.body:
30,000 runners gathered at the Philadelphia Museum of Art for the 2026 Rocky Run Saturday morning.

Fans of the movie "Rocky" retraced the steps of the iconic film character in honor of the movie's 50th anniversary this year.

Actor Scott Teller, who plays "Paulie" in the new film "I Play Rocky" was on hand to cheer on the runners before the race

The 5K race got underway at 7 a.m., and the 10-mile race began at 8 a.m.

Some participants ran both races to complete the 13.1-mile Italian Stallion Challenge.

Each person who completed the race received a medal to celebrate their accomplishment.

All roads that were closed for the race have since reopened.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III fantasy football replacements with Chiefs star out with injury
articles.summary: Who can you add in fantasy football with Kenneth Walker III out on Sunday?
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs will be without superstar running back Kenneth Walker III on Sunday in Atlanta against the Falcons as he heals from a groin injury sustained on Thursday in practice.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the team wanted to "give [Walker] a week" to recover and keep him fresh for the second half of the season. From all accounts, this does not sound like a serious injury.

However, if Walker has been your bright and shining star in your fantasy lineup, who should you turn to next?

Rookie running back Emmett Johnson should get the bulk of carries in Walker's stead, having already totaled 111 yards and a touchdown so far this season. If he's available in your league, go and get him ASAP.

Other than Johnson, running back Jaydn Ott and former Falcons running back Nathan Carter should be available for Kansas City on Sunday. They're both worth gambles if you're really in a bind.

Other than that, get Johnson if you can. Replacing Walker won't be easy, but those are your options.

What is the depth chart with Walker out?

Johnson, Ott, Carter (practice squad elevation)

articles.title: Michigan football to play both Tommy Carr, Bryce Underwood vs Oregon
articles.summary: "You will see Bryce at some point in the game," Kyle Whittingham said on radio. "Can't tell you exactly when... it's not scripted out, it's by feel."
articles.body:
Michigan football will play both Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood against Oregon today .

Coach Kyle Whittingham said on the pregame radio the plan is for Carr, a true freshman, to start a fourth consecutive game, but U-M will bring Underwood into the game at some point. From there, whomever plays better could see the bulk of the snaps.

"Tommy Carr will take the first snap," Whittingham told team play-by-play voice Doug Karsch before Saturday's kickoff. "You will see Bryce at some point in the game. Can't tell you exactly when because it's not scripted out, it's by feel. Then when they both start getting some action, if one of them is hot, we'll stick with that guy.

"if not, we'll try to continue to get both playing

Underwood was the starting quarterback through six games but was benched at halftime at home against Penn State after the Wolverines were shutout and turned the ball over twice in five drives. Carr came in for his first legitimate action in the second half and helped lead the Wolverines to a comeback 21-18 victory.

Carr has since started the past three games − Indiana, at Rutgers and Michigan State − but U-M is just 1-2 in those games and was shutout at halftime in both of the home starts.

Underwood has been a vocal and visible supporter of Carr on the sideline, and remains a team captain.

"His attitude through this whole thing has been terrific," Whittingham said. "You couldn't ask for more of a team guy, team mentality than what Bryce has demonstrated since we made the change. He practices hard, he's leading the team and everything in the warmups, you name it. He's acting as a captain should act, even though it's got to be very frustrating for him, and and has been a challenging time.

"He couldn't have responded any better than he has, and we're really hoping that when he gets his opportunity, that he will make the most of it and have success."

Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia .
